newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends firm after early tumble on APIs.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends firm after early tumble on APIs.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures shrugged off early losses on Wednesday prompted by disappointing U.S. inventory data to end firmer on a wave of short-covering, dealers said.
August Brent, which tested support at $18.50 a barrel in early dealing, closed 12 cents firmer at $18.92 after touching a high of $18.96.
After running up smartly on Tuesday in anticipation of bullish U.S. data, modest losses had been expected from the open given the smaller than expected draw in key refining regions.
"Excluding PADD 5, it was a very small draw," said a broker.
Light profit-taking after three straight sessions of gains also contributed to the early losses, dealers said.

But with a long weekend fast approaching in the U.S. -- NYMEX markets are shut Friday for the Independence Day holiday -- several players including institutional investors were keen to cover their short positions, they said.
Monday's news of maintenance work at Tosco's Bayway refinery this month and its potential impact on gasoline supply was continuing to provide additional support.
Despite Brent's recovery, however, some brokers saw little reason for the complex generally to move higher with the gasoline season peaking and U.S. distillate stocks soaring.
Distillate inventories, comprising heating oil and diesel, rose by a larger than expected four million barrels last week.
"Distillates are looking very bearish," said a broker.
Nevertheless, U.S. heating oil held steady, helping IPE gas oil to a close just off session highs. July gas oil shed just 25 cents to close at $167.50 a tonne after dipping to $166.00.
A firm European spot market, where differentials have been strengthening steadily since the start of the week, also bouyed gas oil sentiment, dealers said.
